2.25.6.en: The discourse here applies to the kingdom of the Romans (58 B.C.-76 B.C.). For the Macedonian kingdom was divided into four parts after the death of Alexander, and the Romans subdued the four parts. The Caesars of Rome were called iron as a sign of their cruelty, which surpassed the cruelty of the kings of the previous kingdoms, just as they were far stronger than the previous empires. The mixing of iron with clay signifies the absence of true unity, and it also signifies corruption.

2.25.7.en: Since the Roman state did not colonize the Holy Land until 63 B.C., the rationalist scholars, who reject divine inspiration and prophecies, claim that the Book of Daniel was written in the period of the Maccabees, about 167-165 B.C., and that the writer does not prophesy but only records earlier historical facts concerning the four kingdoms: the Chaldean, the Median, the Persian, and the Greek. For if they accepted the idea that the fourth kingdom is the Roman state, the writer would have prophesied about it about 100 years before it arose. We have already seen what the evidence confirms, that the writer is in fact the prophet Daniel in the sixth century B.C., not only before the rise of the Roman state but also before the rise of the Greek state.

2.25.8.en: Fr. Abd el-Messih Abu el-Kheir says:

2.25.9.en: a. The Roman armies were known as the iron armies, and the prophet Daniel used the word "iron" 14 times in describing this empire. Hence the Church believed from its dawn that this empire is the Roman Empire. This was the opinion of the earliest Fathers whose writings on the Book of Daniel have reached us, such as St. Irenaeus in the second century AD, St. Hippolytus in the third century, St. Jerome in the fourth century, and Chrysostom, also in the fourth century (347-403 AD). One of the commentators, called Joseph Mede (Joseh Mede), says: [The Jewish Church before the time of our Savior believed that the fourth empire in the Book of Daniel was the Roman Empire, and this belief was received by the disciples of the Apostles and by the whole Christian Church for 300 years].

2.25.10.en: b. What also proves the soundness of this interpretation, and therefore the miraculous character of the inspiration and prophecy in the Book of Daniel, and the greatness of the Holy Bible and that it is the word of God, is that the kingdom of the Messiah, the awaited Christ, began in the days of this empire, for the prophecy says in the dream and the vision: "And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people." The Lord Christ was born in the days of this empire, and His birth took place in Bethlehem because of the command of its Caesar, for the inspired word in the New Testament, at the beginning of the Gospel of St. Luke, says: "And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed" (Lk 2:10), and it dates the beginning of the ministry of John the Baptist, the messenger of Christ, by the dates of its emperor and its governors: "Now in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being governor of Judaea... the word of God came unto John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness" (Lk 3:1-3). The Lord Christ paid taxes to it for Himself and for His disciples (Mt 17:24-27), He dealt in its coinage (Mt 22:17-21), and He was crucified according to its laws (Jn 19:21).

2.25.11.en: c. The Roman Empire was more enduring than the empires that preceded it, for the Babylonian Empire lasted 70 years, the Medo-Persian Empire 200 years, and the Greek Empire 130 years, but the Roman Empire lasted and endured 500 years as a united and undivided empire, and it continued in its two parts, eastern and western, until 1453 AD when the Turks took Constantinople, and the western part continued through the rest of the countries of Europe to this day, and these countries carried their civilizations and a large part of their peoples to the Americas and Australia after their discovery, until these became parts of them.

2.25.12.en: d. St. Irenaeus says in the second century, in his interpretation of the saying of the prophecy "the kingdom shall be divided," and in his reference to the ten toes: "The ten toes, then, are the ten kings into whom the kingdom will be divided, and some of them will be strong and active, and others lazy and useless, but they will agree." And St. Jerome says: [He observes that the prophecy was fulfilled in his own time partly in the destruction of the empire by internal enmity and civil wars. It was fulfilled afterward in the division into an eastern empire and a western empire, and it was fulfilled finally in its division into many small provinces]. St. Hippolytus sees that the ten toes, of iron and of clay, mean the democracies that were rising and divided among the ten toes of the statue, in which the iron would be mixed with the clay.

2.25.13.en: g. Some see that the mixing of iron with clay signifies the mixing of the elements of two distinct civilizations, the entry of the barbarian peoples into the heart of the civilized empire and the barbarians' adoption of the forms of civilization. Hence the invasion of the Germanic tribes on the one hand and of the Turks on the other is an interpretation closer to the true meaning of the symbol in the prophecy.

2.26.0.en: "34 Thou sawest till that a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces. 35 Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken to pieces together, and became like the chaff of the summer threshingfloors; and the wind carried them away, that no place was found for them.

2.26.1.en: And the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth. 36 This is the dream; and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king." [34-36].

2.26.2.en: The most important thing in the dream is this wonderful stone, able to shatter these kingdoms in order to establish a spiritual kingdom that fills the earth, a kingdom that stands forever. Here he speaks of a new kingdom established by the stone cut out without hands, for the Lord Christ came not from the seed of man, but born of the Virgin.

2.26.3.en: The expression "not by hands" points to the nature of His kingdom, that it is not human but heavenly and divine, with no beginning.

2.26.4.en: The Lord Christ is called the stone or the rock because He is the cornerstone who joined the Jews with the Gentiles in one faith, that is, He bound them together as two walls joined by the cornerstone. He is the stone upon which His Church is founded. It was said of Him:

2.26.5.en: "The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. This is the LORD's doing; it is marvellous in our eyes" (Ps 118:22-23). The prophet Isaiah calls Him: "a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to the children of Israel" (Isa 8:14), and "a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation" (Isa 28:16). And the prophet Zechariah says: "For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes" (Zech 3:9; see Acts 4:11; 1 Pet 2:7-8).

2.26.6.en: * After this it remains that "the stone comes from heaven, which smote the image (the statue) and terrified it and shattered all the kingdoms, and gives the Kingdom to the saints of the Most High God.

2.26.7.en: * The stone that smites the image and breaks it in pieces, which fills the whole earth, is Christ, who came from heaven and brought judgment upon the world.

2.26.8.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome * For this reason also, when Daniel saw His coming beforehand, he said that a stone cut out without hands comes into the world. For this is what "without hands" means, that His coming into this world is not accomplished by human work, that is, by the work of those who are accustomed to cut stones. Joseph had no part in it; Mary alone cooperated with the plan (divine) that had been prepared beforehand. This stone, which is from the earth, was found by the power and wisdom of God. Therefore Isaiah also says: "Behold, I lay in Zion a stone... a precious corner stone, a sure foundation" (Isa 28:16). Thus, then, we understand that His coming in human nature was not accomplished by the will of man but by the will of God.

2.26.9.en: St. Irenaeus * This mountain signifies the kingdom of the Jews, and from this mountain He was cut out, where Christ was born. When he says "without hands" we understand that it is without any human work, because works are known by the hands.

2.26.10.en: Father Caesarius * This is the temple of the body that was taken and cut out of the mountain of human nature and the substance of the body, and that without hands, that is, without the work of men.

2.26.11.en: Origen * A great stone was placed upon the well (Gen 29), where many shepherds were accustomed to roll it away when they came together, and then they would give water to themselves and to their flocks. But Jacob alone rolled the stone away and watered the flocks of his bride... What is this stone placed there but Christ Himself...? Daniel also says: "a stone cut out without hands," who is Christ, born without the (seed of a) man. It is a new and wonderful thing that a stone should be cut from the rock without an axe or tools for cutting stones; so, above all wonder, an offspring should appear from a virgin who had not married.

2.27.0.en: 37 "Thou, O king, art a king of kings: for the God of heaven hath given thee a kingdom, power, and strength, and glory. 38 And wheresoever the children of men dwell, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the heaven hath he given into thine hand, and hath made thee ruler over them all. Thou art this head of gold. 39 And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee, and another third kingdom of brass, which shall bear rule over all the earth. 40 And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron: forasmuch as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things: and as iron that breaketh all these, shall it break in pieces and bruise. 41 And whereas thou sawest the feet and toes, part of potters' clay, and part of iron, the kingdom shall be divided; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron, forasmuch as thou sawest the iron mixed with miry clay. 42 And as the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken. 43 And whereas thou sawest iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay. 44 And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever. 45 Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure."

2.27.2.en: and we will tell the interpretation thereof before the king.

2.27.3.en: And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.

2.27.4.en: Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold;

2.27.5.en: the great God hath made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter:

2.27.6.en: and the dream is certain, and the interpretation thereof sure." [36-45].

2.28.0.en: 46 "Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face, and worshipped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an oblation and sweet odours unto him. 47 The king answered unto Daniel, and said, Of a truth it is, that your God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, seeing thou couldest reveal this secret. 48 Then the king made Daniel a great man, and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon."

2.28.1.en: "Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face, and worshipped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an oblation and sweet odours unto him" [46].

2.28.2.en: It was no easy matter for Nebuchadnezzar to fall down and worship Daniel, he who counted himself like a god, to whom all men bow down; especially since Daniel had not brought him joyful news but had affirmed to him that his kingdom would pass away. Yet the king felt his great weakness before the work of God and His plan. The king bowed down in humility, glorifying the God of Daniel, but only for a time, as Pharaoh did before (Ex 9:27; 10:16). Nebuchadnezzar himself touched the mighty hand of God and bore witness to it and declared: "How great are the signs of the Most High God, and how mighty are His wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and His dominion is from generation to generation," but he lost this when he became bound to the love of vain glory, and in a life of luxury the thorns choked the word that had sprung up in him.

2.28.3.en: "The king answered unto Daniel, and said:

2.29.0.en: Of a truth it is, that your God is a God of gods, and a Lord of kings, and a revealer of secrets, seeing thou couldest reveal this secret" [47].

2.29.1.en: He glorified God, but only for a time, since he did not take serious steps for the salvation of his soul. God permitted this to encourage the captive Jews, that they might realize that God is able to be glorified in them if they return to Him with all their hearts.

2.30.0.en: "Then the king made Daniel a great man, and gave him many great gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men of Babylon" [48].

2.30.1.en: Daniel accepted the king's gift for the sake of serving his people. For this reason he was concerned to appoint the three youths over the affairs of the province of Babylon, knowing that they desired nothing of the honors of this world and its wealth, but he did this for the sake of his brethren the captives.

2.31.0.en: "Then Daniel requested of the king, and he set Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, over the affairs of the province of Babylon:

2.31.1.en: but Daniel sat in the gate of the king." [49].

2.31.2.en: Daniel was at the king's gate as head of the men of the palace, so that his eyes might watch every movement and every person entering the palace. Perhaps this meant that he took charge of judgment in matters that touched the royal palace, since it was the ancient custom that the places of judgment were set up at the gate of the palace.

2.31.3.en: Daniel and his companions did not desire temporal things, but sought the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and God gave them both.

2.31.4.en: * When they asked for heavenly things from the Lord, they received temporal things also from the king.

2.31.6.en: Let me enter into my house!

2.31.7.en: * The king, his men, and his counselors were troubled because of a forgotten dream, but Daniel's soul was not shaken at being exposed to death unjustly!

2.31.8.en: Grant me to enter with Daniel into my house, that I may enter into my inner Jerusalem, to meet You, O God of heaven, with Your angels and Your saints.

2.31.9.en: * You carry me to Your eternal chamber, You reveal to me Your surpassing mysteries, and You grant me a knowledge that delights my soul.

2.31.10.en: Turn my life into a joyful hymn of praise!

2.31.11.en: Instead of being troubled by distress, let my whole being be shaken with rejoicing.

2.31.12.en: * I realize that all the kingdoms of the world are like a metal statue that is shattered.

2.31.13.en: You are the cornerstone; You shatter evil and gather the saints in Yourself!

2.31.14.en: You are the One who declares to the earth the abundance of Your love!

2.31.15.en: Let every statue foreign to You be shattered within me, and establish Your joyful Kingdom within me!
